### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient is a 54-year-old black woman presenting with macrocytic anemia (Hb 10.4 g/dL, VCM 107 fL) and neurological symptoms (asthenia, drowsiness, paresthesias, gait disorder). The negative Coombs test rules out autoimmune hemolytic anemia, while low haptoglobin and elevated LDH suggest hemolysis. The presence of neurological symptoms alongside macrocytic anemia raises suspicion for vitamin B12 deficiency. Parenteral vitamin B12 is the appropriate treatment for this condition, as it addresses both the anemia and the neurological manifestations. Evidence supporting this includes the association of vitamin B12 deficiency with macrocytic anemia and neurological symptoms, confirming the need for vitamin B12 supplementation.
